description: Fill the bands FEAT-002 restored with this exam's own figures, so the 3 affected reports are complete rather than structurally correct and numerically empty. Until this lands, secondary/school-results renders its DIVISION PERFORMANCE SUMMARY band blank and primary/school-results renders its grade matrix, school average, pass/fail, competency, council rank and region rank blank - which is the deliberately safe intermediate state chosen in FEAT-002, never the end state. The figures required are aggregates the backend already computes: ExaMetrics analysis is write-once and SchoolAnalysis / LocationAnalysis are loaded into MnContext by build_mn_context. This feature is backend-only and, like FEAT-006, stops at a commit-ready diff.
steps: Establish what data exists by READING THE MODELS, not by querying. Read app/db/models/exametrics/school_analysis.py and app/db/models/exametrics/location_analysis.py and record which columns or JSONB keys hold: divisions split by sex (for the secondary band's SEX x I/II/III/IV/0 with F/M/T); grade counts A-E plus ABS with the WAV/WAS/JUMLA split, school average, %PASS (A-D), %FAIL (E), competency band, council rank and region rank (for the primary band). AGENTS.md forbids querying information_schema or pg_catalog and forbids using the database to understand how the system works - the models and the service layer are the source of truth. If a model does not document a JSONB key's shape, say so rather than guessing; backend-sis/docs/exametrics-processing-pipeline.md documents the JSONB structures and is the place to look next.

Check first whether the existing resolvers already produce these aggregates. data.py is 2372 lines of row functions over the same analysis tables and resolve.py::split_totals already peels off a trailing JUMLA / WASTANI aggregate row that the references print in the summary band. If an aggregate is already computed there, route it to the band rather than recomputing it - a second implementation of the same number that can disagree with the first is worse than none.

Add band resolvers only for what is genuinely missing, in resolve.py alongside ROW_QUERIES, declaratively and per report. Follow the module's existing discipline: it 'adds no aggregation of its own' beyond naming which data function supplies the rows. If a band needs an aggregate no resolver computes, add it to data.py where the other aggregations live, not to resolve.py and not to service.py.

Wire the bands into service.py's generate path as data['bands'], keyed by the band names the package emits (FEAT-004). A band with no resolver stays absent, which renders blank - so a partially wired report degrades to the FEAT-002 state rather than failing.

Route the split_totals aggregate to its band. With bands addressable this replaces both of the old branches: summary_overrides when the header carried figures, and appending it as a final body row when it did not.

Verify against a real exam WITHOUT restarting anything and WITHOUT HTTP. Write a throwaway script under /tmp that opens an async session, calls build_mn_context(db, exam_id) for an exam that has completed processing, resolves the bands for one school unit, renders through render_report, and writes the PDF to /tmp. Then assert with pymupdf that page 1 carries this exam's figures. Read-only: no INSERT, no UPDATE, no DDL. Delete the script afterwards.

Cross-check the rendered figures against the source rows rather than eyeballing them: the band's F / M / T counts must sum to the school's candidate count, and the division totals must match the same numbers the school's own results rows produce. A band that renders plausible but wrong figures is the failure mode this whole task exists to prevent.

Confirm the primary band's Swahili labels come from the measured reference and were not introduced here. The labels JINSI, DARAJA, WALISAJIRIWA, WAV, WAS, JUMLA, WASTANI WA SHULE, %PASS, %FAIL, KUNDI LA UMAHILRI, NAFASI KIWILAYA and NAFASI KIMKOA are the reference's own text carried through the fixture. AGENTS.md forbids introducing NEW Swahili; reproducing the reference's is correct and required. Add no new Swahili strings in code, comments or docs.
Report which of the 3 reports are fully filled, which are partially filled and which band cells remain blank, with the reason for each. Stop at a commit-ready diff: no restart, no deploy.
acceptance_criteria: The data source for every band cell is documented from the MODELS and the pipeline doc, with any undocumented JSONB shape flagged rather than guessed.
No aggregate is computed twice: anything the existing resolvers already produce is routed, not reimplemented, and any new aggregation lives in data.py.
secondary/school-results renders its division summary band with this exam's F / M / T counts per division, and they reconcile against the school's own candidate count and division totals.
primary/school-results renders its grade matrix, school average, %PASS, %FAIL, competency band, council rank and region rank, or each blank cell is named with the reason it is blank.
The split_totals aggregate lands in its band, and neither summary_overrides nor the append-as-body-row branch exists any more.
Verification was done by direct import against a real processed exam, read-only, with the script under /tmp and deleted afterwards - no restart, no HTTP, no DDL, no write of any kind.
No new Swahili appears in code, comments or docs; the reference's own labels are reproduced from the fixture.
A per-report fill status is recorded in findings.
verification: grep -rn "JINSI\|WASTANI\|KIMKOA" /root/apis/backend-sis/app/ ; echo 'expect no NEW Swahili literals introduced by this feature'

school_results_layout_constraints.source: Stated by the user 2026-09-23. These override a literal reading of 'pagination is the reference's' for this report, and they apply to the generated artifact, not to reproducing the reference.
school_results_layout_constraints.blue_background_spans_all_data: The blue background belongs to the WHOLE report wherever there is data - not only to the reference's own filled rows. A generated report with fewer candidates than the reference's 491 must carry the background across its own data extent. Do not inherit the fill row-by-row from the measurement in a way that leaves a generated report's shorter table visually truncated, and do not paint it over rows that hold no data.
school_results_layout_constraints.trailing_sections_must_not_be_forced_ont: The final table (the DIVISION PERFORMANCE SUMMARY / subject analysis sections, measured on pages 14-15) must NOT necessarily start a new page. It should follow immediately after the table that precedes it. The reference puts it on page 14 only because 491 candidates filled 13 pages first; a school with 44 candidates ends its candidate table partway down page 2 and the section belongs right there, not on a page of its own. So section placement is FLOW-relative to the end of the data, while the section's own grid, band and typography stay as measured.
school_results_layout_constraints.consequence_for_verification: The round-trip test in docs/06 section 5 asserts page counts equal, which holds only when the caller supplies exactly the reference's row count. Once sections flow, a generated report legitimately has fewer pages than the reference. Keep the strict round trip as the fixture-equality test (same rows in, same document out) and verify flowed section placement separately, by asserting the section starts on the page and at the offset where the data ended.
